articles.title: The next developer interface is ambient intelligence
articles.excerpt: AI, agents, voice, and physical controls are shifting software development from operating tools to expressing intent—and helping developers stay focused on building. The post The next developer interface is ambient intelligence appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools changed, but the relationship did not. Like most developers, I learned commands, memorized shortcuts, and adapted my thinking to the machine.

AI is changing that relationship and not because I can prompt my way to some workable code. It's more because the system behind it can understand a repository, choose the right model, plan work, use tools, edit files, run commands, inspect failures, and keep going within boundaries the developer controls.

We've made it possible for a developer to describe an outcome, and GitHub Copilot can gather repository context, inspect symbols and dependencies, edit files, run tests, and revise the implementation.
GitHub Copilot coding agent can take an issue into an isolated GitHub Actions-powered environment and return a pull request for review.
It is the shift from issuing commands to making intent executable.

articles.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyone
articles.excerpt: How Cloudflare and OpenAI are working together to help AI find useful content, keep up with changes, and make fewer wasted requests — making the experience better for users and website owners alike.
details: Optimizing your site for AI is of little use if AI can't find it.

The answer to someone's question may already be on your website: the installation guide you spent a week writing, or a first-hand account of using a product, with the details that make the difference for whether they buy it.
As more people turn to AI for help, you want those systems to find your work, represent it accurately, and send interested people your way.

Cloudflare and OpenAI launched a research pilot in July 2026 with those interests in mind. We wanted to find out whether signals from Cloudflare’s network could help ChatGPT users discover new content more efficiently.

Today, we’re sharing early results. So far, the answer is a resounding yes: the pilot has brought previously unknown pages into OpenAI’s search index, giving ChatGPT more sources to draw on to help people find relevant, timely information. Along the way, we’ve learned more about what makes a page worth discovering and how AI systems use the web.

articles.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
articles.excerpt: Introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan, offering eligible academic labs sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind and tools to advance life sciences research.
details: We’re introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan to help more academic scientists access GPT‑Rosalind⁠, our dedicated life sciences model, which combines frontier reasoning with Rosalind workbench that enables specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance, and other scientific applications.
Eligible labs can receive up to 30 Business Standard seats at no cost for up to 12 months, with access to GPT‑Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval.
Academic research creates knowledge that entire fields build on.
Work that begins with a fundamental question about biology can eventually change how we diagnose disease, develop medicines, or grow food.
But those advances depend on scientists having the resources to explore ideas, test them, and share what they learn.

articles.title: A fully programmable secure web gateway
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare Gateway and Data Loss Prevention have inherited the flexibility and power of Cloudflare Workers through our full-stack integration with the Cloudflare Developer platform.
details: Every secure web gateway on the market works the same way: traffic matches a condition. A terminal action fires. Allow, Block, Isolate, Log. This model has been the foundation of network security for nearly 30 years, and it handles the common case well. But it has a ceiling, and customers with complex environments hit that ceiling regularly.
Earlier this year, we shared our vision to build a truly programmable SASE platform .
We also outlined how the term programmability has become diluted by the security industry.
Most vendors claim programmability because they have public APIs, Terraform providers, webhooks, and alerting.
Cloudflare offers all of those things too, but that’s not enough.

articles.title: Deploy with Void
articles.excerpt: Introducing Void: an open-source SDK, CLI, and self-hosted platform for building full-stack Vite apps and deploying them to Cloudflare.
details: VoidZero's tools such as Vite, Vitest, Oxc, and Rolldown - bundled in one toolchain as Vite+ - have made frontend development faster, but building full-stack applications requires more than just a tooling stack. These applications need server routes, databases, local development environments, and a fast and easy way to deploy ideas to production.
We’re excited to open-source three new products that bring server routing, typed data access, and Cloudflare deployment into a unified Vite workflow.
Void Platform: A shared deployment platform for teams to host Void apps on Cloudflare.
Void SDK: A composable JavaScript SDK for building full-stack apps with Vite.
Void CLI: A CLI for provisioning resources and deploying Vite apps to Cloudflare.

articles.title: Yandex outage: Data shows that instead of going dark, malicious bots went on the move
articles.excerpt: When strikes hit Yandex data centers, many assumed Russian bot operations went dark. Cloudflare data reveals that while search crawling stopped, malicious bots simply migrated to other networks.
details: Following reported strikes on Yandex data centers, claims circulated on the Internet that Russian bot farms and influence operations had been knocked offline.
HTTP traffic charts showed steep drops, fueling speculation that the infrastructure damage had stopped these malicious actors.
There are two autonomous system numbers ( ASNs ) associated with Yandex: AS13238 is used by Yandex’s search engine, while AS200350 runs its cloud services.
Using Cloudflare Radar and Bot Management data, we analyzed how these two ASNs were affected - and while both saw drops in traffic, they saw differing impact.
Yandex Search (AS13238) : The drop in traffic consisted almost entirely of verified search crawlers indexing web pages, images, and site resources.

articles.title: Why Is My Kubernetes Job Still Pending? Tracing Kueue Admission with Headlamp
articles.excerpt: You submit a Kubernetes Job and wait for its Pods to appear. A minute passes. Then another. The Job is still suspended, there are no application logs, and there may not even be a Pod to inspect. In a cluster managed by Kueue , this can be completely normal. Kueue may still be deciding whether the Job can use…
details: In a cluster managed by Kueue , this can be completely normal. Kueue may still be deciding whether the Job can use the requested resources. The useful question is not only “Why is the Pod pending?” It is first “Has Kueue admitted the Workload?”

The Kueue plugin for Headlamp brings that investigation into the Headlamp UI. Instead of reconstructing the admission path from several commands and large YAML objects, you can begin with the Workload, read its condition message, and follow links through the LocalQueue, ClusterQueue, ResourceFlavor, and Cohort.
This article follows that Headlamp-first path. The command line appears only in a short optional section for reproducing the example.

You need a Kubernetes cluster with Kueue installed , a Headlamp installation , and the 0.1.0-alpha Kueue plugin . Your Kubernetes identity must be allowed to read the Kueue resources used in this article.

The alpha release provides read-only views for Kueue v1beta2 Cohorts, ClusterQueues, LocalQueues, ResourceFlavors, and Workloads. It does not add its own create, edit, stop, resume, or delete workflows. Headlamp still provides its standard YAML and resource actions where your permissions allow them.

articles.title: SentinelOne cuts malware analysis from weeks to hours
articles.excerpt: With OpenAI Daybreak, SentinelOne cuts weeks of malware analysis to hours, creating capacity to investigate more threats.
details: Reverse engineering a sophisticated piece of malware can take a top security researcher four to six weeks.
It’s painstaking work where researchers pull apart software to understand how it behaves, often retracing their steps as they uncover new information.
Gregor Stewart, Chief AI Officer at SentinelOne, says OpenAI Daybreak can now produce human-level reverse-engineering output in roughly eight hours.
By reducing the time needed for deep analysis, OpenAI gives SentinelOne’s researchers room to investigate more malware and connect findings across samples.
That wider view often reveals relationships that isolated investigations might miss.

articles.title: How Third Moment Research runs 10,000 agents for 36+ hours
articles.excerpt: With GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, Codex, and Daybreak for cybersecurity, this AI lab builds agents that focus for days and improve with use.
details: Every company has its own workflows, tools, edge cases, and definitions of success.Third Moment Research believes the best agents should be really good at that specific work and should improve their capabilities the more they’re used.

The company is building a self-improving AI system around that idea, using OpenAI’s latest models to understand agent behavior, identify recurring weaknesses, and automatically create thousands of synthetic scenarios around those problems.
The team uses those scenarios to improve agents, repeating the process as new issues emerge.
Codex, GPT‑6 Astra, GPT‑6 Sol, and GPT‑6.1 Sol support the system’s research and computational work, enabling Third Moment to run 10,000 agents at once on investigations lasting 36-48 hours.
This domain provides a concrete setting to study how agents work and where they struggle.

articles.title: How Block is building AI-powered security with OpenAI technology
articles.excerpt: Block is building AI-powered security with OpenAI. Its security team investigates threats faster and proposes patches in minutes.
details: At Block, the company behind Square, Cash App, and Afterpay, the security team leverages the OpenAI Defense Factory: where AI handles vulnerability discovery, detection, and response at a scale that no human team could keep up with.
With AI systems including OpenAI Daybreak, Block is taking just hours to do work that used to take weeks. > “AI is compressing the time from human intent to action.
For a while, it was assumed that there was an attacker advantage since they’re faster and more nimble.

But with things like Daybreak and the advancements in OpenAI’s tooling, defenders are able to fight fire with fire and keep up with the rapid pace of AI adoption.” -James Nettesheim, Chief Information Security Officer, Block Block’s security team has been focused on responsibly adopting AI across workflows, whether that’s code generation or security operations.
“What it’s really centered on is having a new teammate that you can scale with,” James Nettesheim, Chief Information Security Officer, says.

Rust 1.99.1 fixes the following regressions from prior releases:
Missing symbol wcslen : Some Rust targets were getting link errors for missing wcslen , and that function is now present in Rust's compiler-builtins library as a fallback.
The LLVM loop-idiom-wcslen pass may introduce calls to wcslen as an optimization, and some Rust targets did not have that function readily available in libc or elsewhere.

articles.title: Staying Evergreen: How we automated secure access and repo hygiene in a shared org
articles.excerpt: Put native GitHub features to work to review outside collaborator access and archive stale repositories. The post Staying Evergreen: How we automated secure access and repo hygiene in a shared org appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Working with outside collaborators can add more work for a repository owner. You need to confirm who still needs access, change permissions as projects evolve, and archive repositories once they've served their purpose.

To keep up, repository owners need to track collaborators, deadlines, and follow-ups for each repository. As a project grows, that manual housekeeping becomes harder to keep up with and easier to defer.

We faced this problem in a shared organization where GitHub employees ("Hubbers") collaborate with customers and partners on product trials and professional services engagements. Our answer was Evergreen , a GitHub App built with native GitHub features. The workflows below exhibit a pattern you can adapt for your own organization.
Evergreen is a GitHub App that automates organization hygiene through two workflows:
Outside collaborator access reviews. Every quarter, each repo's outside collaborators are reviewed. Keep who you need, and everyone else is removed.

articles.title: GitHub availability report: September 2026
articles.excerpt: In September, we experienced two incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services. The post GitHub availability report: September 2026 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Our last update covered content through August. We did not publish another in September while other public content addressed the August 17 outage. This edition covers progress over the past two months.

The short version of August and September : we reduced shared-database pressure, added overload controls, created headroom for GitHub Actions, expanded failure containment for pull requests, and moved more production workloads to Azure. Significant incidents, a capacity pause, and a missed migration target show that the work is not complete.

By October 7, 120 of 160 production services were deployed in Central US, and 13 of 51 primary MySQL databases had moved. Azure also handled 65.4% of read traffic for GitHub's core application, 48.3% of Git read traffic, and 80.2% of stream-processing traffic. These percentages measure different workloads and should not be added.
We paused Central US deployments and traffic increases on September 11 because capacity was uneven across availability zones.
Permanent ramps resumed September 18 after temporary relief, but durable capacity work continues, with a goal of unlocking all available capacity by the end of October.

articles.title: Inside Hyperdrive: How we solved a rare Hyperdrive MySQL caching bug
articles.excerpt: While adding MySQL support to Hyperdrive, we found a subtle protocol bug when caching query results. Here is how we tracked down a 0.001% rate error and made Hyperdrive MySQL generally available.
details: Hyperdrive support for MySQL is now generally available (GA). Hyperdrive , Cloudflare’s database connection pooler for Workers, initially only supported Postgres. Since we announced the beta for MySQL protocol support last year, we have been working on making our MySQL handling as reliable as our Postgres support.
We’ve learned some things from building and running a MySQL connection pooler on Cloudflare’s network. It turns out that the difference between beta and GA is just 20 bug fixes in a trenchcoat.
During the beta, our goal was to validate that real-world customer usage hit our production availability target of 99.99%.
We knew there were gaps in our reliability since we track how often client connections from a Worker end in an error related to Hyperdrive.
In addition, we had feedback from customers in the beta that led to the discovery of a rare and subtle bug in our production environment.
